newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES CONTINUE SLIDE, BOTTOM NOT SEEN.
newsitem.headline: SHARES CONTINUE SLIDE, BOTTOM NOT SEEN.

text.p: Lithuanian shares continued to slide on Monday and dealers said that prices had probably not hit the bottom yet.
"Things don't look good right now and we don't expect any improvement this week," said one dealer.
Only eleven of the 43 A list companies traded on Monday gained. Among the losers, four shed ten percent off their price.

Siauliu Bank was one of them, as it stumbled for the second straight session after a four-day bull run fueled by Hermis Bank's announcement that it planned to acquire 51 percent of its shares. Siauliu eased to 90.00 litas from 100.00 litas.
Hermis Bank lost ground itself, slipping to 175.00 litas to 185.00 litas. Its price has stayed relatively low despite good results for 1996 and the first quarter of this year.
Vilniaus Bank was the only banking share to gain, inching up to 235.00 litas from 232.00 litas, an increase of 1.29 percent.
